# vcraft 1.4.0

**Windows is supported, and a class can now do arithmetic.**

## Highlights

- **Windows (`win_amd64`).** `vcraft build` links the `.pyd` against the interpreter's own
  import library with the MinGW runtime folded in with `-static`, so the wheel imports on a
  machine that has no compiler on `PATH`, and an abi3 extension is named `.pyd`, the only
  suffix the loader will import there. The CLI, `vcraft toolchain install` (through
  `makev.bat`), `vcraft generate-ci` and the action all run on `windows-latest`, and every
  suite — including the previously POSIX-only packaging, wheel, docs and CLI — passes
  there across CPython 3.11–3.15.
- **Numeric operators.** `@[vc_add]` through `@[vc_xor]` fill CPython's number slots, and
  `@[vc_neg]`, `@[vc_pos]`, `@[vc_abs]` and `@[vc_invert]` the unary ones, so a class can
  define `+ - * / // % ** << >> & | ^` and `-x`. An operand is a scalar or another
  instance, and a scalar on the left (`2 + counter`) reaches the reflected function.
- **More types.** An `enum` crosses as a generated `enum.IntEnum` of the same name, a plain
  `struct` as a `dict`, maps take scalar keys, and composites nest — `?[]int`, `[][]int`,
  `map[string][]int` — as parameters and as results.
- **A documentation site.** A guide and a reference, in English and Spanish, at
  <https://rroblf01.github.io/vcraft/>.

## Built with vcraft

[`vqubit`](https://pypi.org/project/vqubit/) is the reference project: a dependency-free
quantum computing framework whose linear algebra, gate matrices and simulators are written
in V, shipped as one abi3 wheel per platform.

## Upgrade

```console
$ pip install --upgrade vcraft
```

No migration is needed: 1.4.0 only adds to the 1.x surface. The full list is in
[CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/rroblf01/vcraft/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md#140---2026-10-16).
